## <a id="extra-passes-at-test-time"></a>Does running more passes at test time than in training keep improving quality?

**mixed** · updated 2026-11-23

Models trained with a sampled or variable number of passes stay flat or improve slightly beyond the training depth, and their gains level off near the training mean. Ouro, trained with 4 steps and learned exits rather than sampled depth, loses accuracy at 5-8 steps. No source trains the same model both ways, so the role of sampled-depth training is not isolated.

| Paper | Stance | Setting | Finding | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Huginn](2502.05171.md) | partly | 3.5B dense, 800B tokens, passes sampled with mean 32 | First-turn MT-Bench is 5.693 at 64 iterations and 5.662 at 32, a difference the paper calls not significant. ARC-C saturates around 8-12 iterations without few-shot examples and around 32 with 25-50 examples. | Table 6; Section 5.3; Figures 7 and 9 |
| [Parcae](2604.12946.md) | partly | 350M (RDM setup) trained with mean 8 passes sampled per sequence; 140M-1.3B models for the saturation result | Validation PPL is 10.09 at T=8 and 10.11 at T=16. Run at up to twice the training mean, the 140M-1.3B models' gains plateau near T = μ_rec. | Table 8; Section 5.3; Figure 7 |
| [Looped CED](2611.13378.md) | partly | 150M CED, 6.0B tokens, rounds sampled from max(1, Poisson(8)) | Running 12 or 16 rounds instead of 8 lowers BPB by at most 0.0004 and never raises it (0.8465 at T=8, 0.8462 at T=12 and 16). | Appendix F; Table 9 |
| [Retrofitted Recurrence](2511.07384.md) | partly | TinyLlama-1.1B retrofitted to (4,8,4), about 50B math tokens | Trained with mean recurrence 4, the model scores 38.0 on GSM8K at test recurrence 4 and 37.9 at 32; trained with mean 16, it scores 43.4 at test recurrence 16 and 43.7 at 32. | Table 3 |
| [Inkling 2 Mini](tml-inkling-2-mini.md) | partly | TML-d24-varloop-research, 26.4B total / 3.4B active MoE, trained with 1-5 passes | Never trained with more than five passes, it keeps a no-CoT 50% time horizon of 40 s at ten passes against 42 s at five, and on N-Hop Lookup it keeps improving out to ten loops. | No-CoT capabilities; figures "No-CoT time horizons" and "N-Hop Lookup" |
| [Ouro (LoopLM)](2510.25741.md) | against | Ouro 1.4B and 2.6B, 7.7T tokens, trained with 4 recurrent steps (8 in the first stage) and learned exit gates | MMLU falls from 67.45 at T=4 to 64.49 at T=8 for the 1.4B model and from 74.60 to 72.24 for the 2.6B model; AIME 2024 for the 1.4B Thinking model falls from 65.00 at T=4 to 38.67 at T=8. Safety on HEx-PHI keeps improving through the extrapolated steps. | Tables 10-13; Section 7.1; Figure 8a |

## <a id="loop-placement"></a>Where in the stack should the loop sit?

**consistent** · updated 2026-11-25

Every comparison favors looping lower or middle layers over the whole stack or the top layers, and in layouts with a shared global KV the loop should include the layers that produce it. The comparisons come from models of 1.7B parameters or less (the 1.7B one finetuned from a pretrained model), or from runs whose sizes are not given.

| Paper | Stance | Setting | Finding | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [SMELT](2609.01343.md) | supports | 200M MoE, FLOPs, parameters and KV matched, two passes | Looping the middle 6 of 12 layers gives validation loss 1.9257 against 1.9322 for looping all 12 (S ≈ 85%), and every span tested beats the unlooped Baseline (1.9445). DCLM Core at S ≈ 95% peaks at the 67% span instead. | Table 3; Section 3.3 |
| [Inkling 2 Mini](tml-inkling-2-mini.md) | supports | Scaling-ladder runs, three passes, equal training compute; model sizes not given | Looping the middle 12 layers beat looping the last 12 on 27 of 28 evaluations; a no-loop baseline would need an estimated 1.51-1.91x the compute to match the middle loop, against 1.24-1.36x for the last loop. | Looping design; figure "Compute-equivalent gain by loop position" |
| [Looped CED](2611.13378.md) | supports | 150M CED, 6.0B and 29.6B tokens | Looping encoder layers L2-5, which contain the global KV source, reaches 0.8468 BPB against 0.8648 for looping decoder layers L7-10 (no loop 0.8716); after 29.6B tokens the decoder loop captures only 38% of the encoder loop's improvement. | Table 1; Table 2 |
| [YOCO-U](2604.01220.md) | supports | 1.3B dense, 20B tokens | Looping the self-decoder averages 48.25 against 47.34 for looping the cross-decoder. At about 2x FLOPs, looping the whole 20-layer Transformer twice averages 47.8 against 48.3 for RINS and YOCO-U. | Table 5; Table 3 |
| [MoR](2507.10524.md) | partly | Fixed-depth recursive models; 730M base with unique parameters fixed at 252M (Nr=3), and 135M base (Nr=2) | Keeping the first and last layers unshared (Middle-Cycle, 1+8+1) beats cycling the whole stack (Cycle, 10 layers) at 252M unique parameters, NLL 2.7552 vs 2.7573 and accuracy 42.32 vs 41.90; at the 135M base with Nr=2, Cycle is slightly ahead (3.0071 vs 3.0330). | Appendix F; Tables 10-11 |
| [LoopRes](2611.31094.md) | supports | Qwen3-1.7B-Base finetuned on 3.1B tokens of math and code SFT data, 2x compute | For Huginn + AttnRes, looping the middle 14 of 28 layers three times averages 53.9 on seven math and code benchmarks, against 50.9 for looping all layers twice at the same 2x compute. | Appendix C.1; Table 12 |

## <a id="more-passes-fixed-compute"></a>With training compute held fixed, do more passes help?

**mixed** · updated 2026-11-23

On language modeling at the budgets tested, SMELT and MoR find two passes better than three or four with FLOPs fixed, and in Ouro the gap to untied models of the same executed depth grows with the step count. Other results point the other way: Parcae's compute-optimal number of passes rises with the training budget, deeper training recurrence pays off per training FLOP for two of three retrofitted model families, and on Ouro's synthetic Mano task more passes of fewer layers win at the same executed depth.

| Paper | Stance | Setting | Finding | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [SMELT](2609.01343.md) | against | 200M MoE, S ≈ 85%, FLOPs, parameters and KV matched (more passes force a narrower model) | Validation loss is 1.9257 at 2 passes, 1.9385 at 3 and 1.9360 at 4; DCLM Core is 27.57, 27.15 and 27.30. | Table 5; Section 3.5 |
| [MoR](2507.10524.md) | against | 360M base, 16.5e18 training FLOPs; more recursions mean fewer unique parameters (167M, 118M, 98M) | Expert-choice MoR reaches validation NLL 2.7511 at Nr=2, 2.7925 at Nr=3 and 2.8204 at Nr=4; fixed-depth recursion gives 2.8079, 2.8466 and 2.8781 (vanilla 2.7824). | Table 3 |
| [Ouro (LoopLM)](2510.25741.md) | against | 53M-1.36B, 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens; untied model with the same executed depth and more unique parameters | The untied model scores higher in every case and the gap grows with the step count; at 1.3B the average benchmark gap is 0.017 at 2 steps and 0.025 at 4. | Appendix D.1; Table 18 |
| [Ouro (LoopLM)](2510.25741.md) | supports | Synthetic Mano task (modular arithmetic), 12 executed layers in every layout, unique parameters differ | At maximum expression length 24, 3 layers looped 4 times reach 92.2 exact-match accuracy, against 78.0 for 2 layers x 6, 35.1 for 6 layers x 2 and 34.8 for 12 unlooped layers. | Section 6.2; Figure 6 (right) |
| [Parcae](2604.12946.md) | partly | 140M and 370M, parameters and training FLOPs fixed (tokens shrink as passes grow) | The compute-optimal mean recurrence rises with the budget, from 2 at 1x10^18 FLOPs to 10 at 64x10^18 for 140M, following a power law with exponent about 0.40; at some small budgets fixed depth scores higher Core (10.5 vs 9.0 at 2x10^18 FLOPs). | Table 6; Section 5.2; Figure 5 |
| [Retrofitted Recurrence](2511.07384.md) | partly | 1B-class models retrofitted from TinyLlama, OLMo and Llama, about 50B math tokens | Per training FLOP, larger training recurrences give a larger GSM8K gain for OLMo and Llama but not for TinyLlama. | Section 4.3.2; Figure 20 |

## <a id="shared-kv-across-passes"></a>Can later passes reuse one KV cache instead of keeping KV for every pass?

**mixed** · updated 2026-11-23

Reusing the last pass's KV works when the model is trained for it or when it is done only during decoding, while reusing the first pass's KV alone costs accuracy unless a local window is added. Looped CED loses nothing with last-round KV under sampled-depth training but fails with fixed depth, Ouro keeps quality with last-step KV in decoding but not in prefill, and PLT needs a gated sliding window on top of first-pass KV sharing.

| Paper | Stance | Setting | Finding | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Looped CED](2611.13378.md) | partly | 150M CED, 6.0B tokens, exact fp32 token-by-token decoding at T=8 | With sampled-depth training, last-round KV changes BPB by -0.0002 relative to per-round KV; with fixed-depth training it adds +0.0317. | Table 3 |
| [Ouro (LoopLM)](2510.25741.md) | partly | Ouro 1.4B, KV reuse during decoding only | Keeping only the last step's KV gives GSM8K 78.85 and MATH-500 80.40 against 78.92 and 82.40 with all four caches, at 4.00x less memory; first-step-only KV drops to 18.73 and 8.43, and reusing KV during prefill costs more than 10 points on GSM8K. | Section 5.4.2; Table 14 |
| [PLT](2510.24824.md) | partly | 680M activated / 13B total MoE, 150B tokens | Sharing the first loop's KV halves the KV cache (560M to 280M) but lowers average accuracy from 39.6 to 36.2; adding gated SWA with a 64-token window restores 39.7 at 284M. | Table 2 |
| [YOCO-U](2604.01220.md) | supports | 1.3B dense, 20B tokens | Looping the cross-decoder while it keeps reading the one shared global KV averages 47.34, against 46.41 when those layers use their own self-attention KV instead. | Table 5; Section 4.3 |
| [MoR](2507.10524.md) | partly | 360M-base family, 10B FineWeb-Edu tokens | Recursive KV sharing, which reuses the first recursion's KV, raises validation NLL for expert-choice MoR from 2.8667 to 2.8895 but lowers it for token-choice MoR from 2.9358 to 2.9155. | Section 4.3; Table 15 |
| [Huginn](2502.05171.md) | supports | Huginn 3.5B, zero-shot (not trained for it), first-turn MT-Bench | Capping the per-token KV cache at s=4, 8 or 16 recurrence steps scores 5.856, 5.631 and 5.687 against 5.662 for the full cache at 32 iterations; the paper finds no significant difference. | Table 6; Section 6.2 |
